La personne titulaire du poste de directeur ou directrice principal·e, Technologies, Stratégie et opérations collabore étroitement avec le directeur général, Architecture technologique et le directeur de la Technologie du STI. Elle traduit la stratégie, les priorités et les feuilles de route en activités coordonnées à l’échelle de l’équipe. Elle assure la coordination centrale de l’architecture technologique et veille à ce que les activités liées à l’architecture, à la mise en œuvre et aux opérations soient harmonisées et bien coordonnées et progressent efficacement. De plus, elle structure les priorités de la fonction, en assure la visibilité et en suit l’avancement, tout en respectant les responsabilités établies à l’égard de la stratégie technologique, des décisions relatives à l’architecture et de la gouvernance officielle des projets et des programmes.
  
  
**Ce que vous ferez**

* Soutenir la direction de l’architecture technologique dans la mise en œuvre des stratégies, des priorités et des feuilles de route établies en les traduisant en activités et jalons, et en définissant clairement les dépendances et les responsabilités à l’échelle de la fonction
* Maintenir une vue d’ensemble des priorités et des activités de l’architecture technologique pour soutenir la planification et la prise de décisions de la direction
* Appuyer l’analyse, la planification et la coordination des priorités émergentes et des initiatives spéciales en reliant les plans d’architecture technologique aux priorités globales du STI et du cabinet
* Servir de point de coordination central entre les activités liées à l’architecture, au développement, à la mise en œuvre et aux opérations, y compris pour ce qui touche les dépendances, le séquencement des tâches, les décisions et les transferts entre les architectes, les responsables techniques et les équipes de mise en œuvre
* Veiller à ce que les décisions et les priorités en matière d’architecture soient prises en compte dans la planification et l’exécution de la mise en œuvre
* Participer à la coordination des activités d’architecture technologique entre les différentes fonctions, ainsi qu’à l’échelle du cabinet canadien et de l’organisation mondiale
* Établir des modes de fonctionnement efficaces qui aident l’équipe à gérer les priorités, les décisions, les risques, les mesures à prendre et les dépendances, et à assurer le suivi des mesures et des engagements convenus
* Repérer les occasions de simplifier les processus, d’améliorer les méthodes de travail et de renforcer la coordination au sein de l’équipe
* Fournir à la direction une vision intégrée des besoins, des activités et des dépendances pour appuyer une planification efficace des ressources et des priorités
* Appuyer la coordination et la réalisation des initiatives d’architecture technologique en établissant clairement les résultats, les jalons, les responsables, les dépendances et les risques, en particulier lorsque le travail nécessite la collaboration des équipes d’architecture et de mise en œuvre
* Travailler de concert avec le bureau de gestion de projets et les gestionnaires de projet désignés pour les initiatives nécessitant une gouvernance officielle, et porter à l’attention de la direction les risques, les contraintes et les décisions exigeant son intervention
* Fournir à la direction de l’architecture technologique des mises à jour concises axées sur la prise de décisions concernant les priorités, les progrès, les risques et les enjeux
* Assurer la coordination avec les autres équipes du STI au pays et ailleurs dans le monde, les directeurs de la Technologie des différentes fonctions et les parties prenantes concernées pour atteindre les objectifs en matière d’architecture technologique
* Préparer et animer des séances de planification d’équipe, des revues de direction, des séances de travail et d’autres rencontres de coordination; communiquer clairement les questions techniques et les enjeux liés à la réalisation des initiatives aux parties prenantes techniques et non techniques

**Ce que vous apportez au rôle**

* Baccalauréat en informatique, en génie, en systèmes d’information, en gestion des technologies, en affaires ou dans un domaine connexe (ou expérience pratique équivalente)
* Expérience considérable dans des environnements technologiques, idéalement dans les domaines de la prestation de services technologiques, de l’optimisation de l’architecture, des opérations technologiques ou des domaines connexes
* Compréhension approfondie des environnements technologiques d’entreprise et de la relation entre l’architecture, la mise en œuvre et les activités courantes, ainsi que des connaissances techniques suffisantes pour comprendre les concepts d’architecture, les dépendances, les considérations relatives à la mise en œuvre et les risques liés à la prestation, sans nécessairement être spécialiste technique
* Solides compétences en stratégie et en opérations, notamment en matière de planification, de priorisation, de coordination, d’analyse et de présentation de l’information aux dirigeants.
* Expérience de la coordination d’initiatives technologiques complexes faisant intervenir plusieurs équipes, parties prenantes et dépendances
* Grand sens de l’organisation, excellent jugement et fortes aptitudes en communication; capacité à structurer, à clarifier et à faire progresser des travaux complexes ou ambigus, et à travailler efficacement avec des leaders en technologie, des architectes, des spécialistes techniques et des professionnels de la gestion de projet

As a Project Quality Manager, you will be responsible for leading and managing the overall Quality Assurance and Quality Control function for the project, ensuring that all project activities comply with contractual requirements, approved specifications, applicable standards and client expectations.

The role offers significant exposure to all aspects of quality management within large-scale Data Centre construction projects, providing opportunities to develop multidisciplinary expertise across Mechanical, Electrical and CSA disciplines. * Establish project quality objectives, KPIs, inspection requirements and reporting processes.

* Coordinate with design, BIM, engineering, procurement and construction teams to integrate quality requirements throughout project delivery.
* Oversee material quality management, including approvals, receiving inspections, traceability, storage and preservation.

The Transportation Manager is responsible for the safe, compliant, and cost-effective operation of the company's transportation fleet, ensuring reliable service to customers while supporting overall business objectives. This role oversees driver performance, regulatory compliance, transportation operations, and budget management to maximize fleet utilization, control costs, and maintain the highest standards of safety and service.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

**Transportation Operations**

* Manage the daily operation of the company's transportation fleet to ensure safe, timely, and cost-effective delivery of products.
* Develop and optimize delivery routes, schedules, dispatch processes, and transportation workflows.
* Coordinate transportation activities with warehouse, production, sales, and customer service teams to meet business and customer requirements.
* Monitor service performance and implement corrective actions to improve delivery reliability, fleet utilization, and operational efficiency.
* Coordinate third-party transportation providers when internal fleet capacity is unavailable.

**Fleet Maintenance & Asset Management**

* Oversee the maintenance, inspection, repair, and overall condition of tractors, trailers, refrigeration units, and transportation equipment.
* Ensure preventive maintenance programs are executed to maximize equipment reliability, safety, and uptime.
* Monitor fleet performance, fuel consumption, maintenance expenses, downtime, and asset utilization.
* Manage equipment records, licensing, registrations, inspections, and asset lifecycle planning, including replacement and capital recommendations.
* Coordinate internal and external service providers to ensure efficient and cost-effective fleet support.

**Driver Leadership, Safety & Compliance**

* Recruit, train, develop, and supervise CDL drivers and transportation personnel.
* Establish performance expectations and maintain accountability for safety, productivity, attendance, and customer service.
* Administer and enforce company policies and collective bargaining agreement provisions in a fair, consistent, and compliant manner.
* Develop and implement strategies to attract, retain, and engage qualified transportation personnel.
* Ensure compliance with DOT, FMCSA, food safety, temperature-control, union, and company transportation requirements.
* Maintain driver qualification files, ELD compliance, hours-of-service records, licensing, certifications, and vehicle inspection documentation.
* Investigate accidents, incidents, violations, and customer complaints, implementing corrective actions as appropriate.
* Lead transportation safety programs, driver development initiatives, and regulatory audit readiness efforts.

**Financial Management & Continuous Improvement**

* Develop and manage the transportation budget, including labor, fuel, maintenance, insurance, capital expenditures, and outside transportation expenses.
* Monitor transportation KPIs and prepare reports for leadership regarding operational performance, safety, service levels, and cost management.
* Identify and implement opportunities to improve efficiency, limit driver overtime, reduce costs, increase fleet utilization, and enhance customer service.
* Oversee transportation technology including fleet management systems, telematics, GPS tracking, dash cameras, and ELD platforms.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Business, Logistics, Transportation, Supply Chain, or a related field preferred; equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered.
* Minimum of 5–7 years of transportation or fleet management experience, preferably in food distribution, food service, or a high-volume delivery environment.
* Minimum of 3 years of supervisory or management experience.
* Experience managing employees in a unionized environment, including working within collective bargaining agreement requirements.
* Strong knowledge of DOT and FMCSA regulations and transportation safety requirements.
* Experience managing CDL drivers, fleet maintenance, dispatching, and route optimization.
* Demonstrated experience managing budgets, controlling costs, and improving operational performance.
* Strong problem-solving, organizational, and decision-making skills.
* Excellent communication and leadership abilities.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office and transportation management systems (TMS).

* Valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record.
* Candidate must successfully pass post-offer/pre-employment drug and background screen.

**Physical Requirements**

* Ability to sit, stand, and walk for extended periods throughout the workday.
* Ability to regularly inspect tractors, trailers, refrigeration units, and transportation equipment in warehouse, yard, and outdoor environments.
* Ability to bend, kneel, crouch, reach, and climb stairs or ladders during equipment inspections and facility walkthroughs.
* Ability to occasionally lift and carry up to 25 pounds and move transportation-related materials or supplies.
* Ability to work in varying environmental conditions, including heat, cold, rain, and other outdoor weather conditions.
* Ability to respond to transportation emergencies, accidents, breakdowns, or operational issues outside of normal business hours when required.

**Work Environment**

* Work is performed in a combination of office, warehouse, loading dock, maintenance shop, and outdoor environments.

**Head of Engineering Job Description:** Scope, Impact & Qualifications Reports to: CEO Level: Executive (CTO-equivalent scope) Org size: ~25 engineers Time split: 70% Product / 30% Discipline ROLE SUMMARY The Head of Engineering owns the technical outcomes of Maestro's entire product suite while also serving as the top of the engineering discipline ladder: every engineering manager and individual contributor ultimately ladders up to this role. The position deliberately splits attention: 70% product execution, 30% discipline accountability. Product delivery is the immediate, ongoing accountability; discipline work compounds over time and requires protected but smaller blocks of focus so it doesn't get crowded out by delivery pressure. This role sits at the center of Maestro's matrix structure, accountable for craft quality and standards company-wide, while ensuring embedded engineering talent on each product team is pointed at the right priorities.
  
  
**SCOPE • Org reach:** all engineering leads across all product lines report into this role (directly or via a lead layer), the senior-most engineering accountability in the company. • Product surface: full product suite, every active product line's engineering output. • Discipline surface: engineering-wide standards, tooling, and process, independent of which product team an engineer sits on. THE 70%: PRODUCT ACCOUNTABILITY The Head of Engineering is the single accountable owner for engineering execution across Maestro's product portfolio.
  
  
**What this looks like day to day:** • Partners with the engineering leads of every product line to ensure their teams are resourced against the right priorities: not just busy, but correctly sequenced. • Accountable for ensuring product strategy and roadmap direction are translated into clear, actionable engineering plans, serving as the connective layer between Product and Delivery leadership and the engineering organization, primarily through engineering leads embedded within product teams. • Accountable for applying technical judgment to turn high-level strategic priorities into concrete technical execution plans, enabling and guiding engineering leads to scope, sequence, and de-risk delivery across their product areas. • Identifies where product priorities and engineering capacity are misaligned across teams and resolves the tradeoff, including cross-team resourcing calls.
  
  

* Is the escalation point when a product line's engineering execution is off track, and is accountable for getting it back on track. Impact: Every product line ships against strategy, not just against what's easiest to build. Product and Delivery leaders have one accountable engineering partner instead of negotiating separately with each product line's lead. THE 30%: DISCIPLINE ACCOUNTABILITY The Head of Engineering owns what "good engineering" means at Maestro, independent of the product line.

**What this looks like day to day:** • Sets and maintains company-wide engineering standards (code quality, architecture principles, technical debt posture). • Owns cross-cutting technical initiatives that no single product team should solve independently, e.g. product suite services and universal QA automation. • Defines how AI tooling is used across engineering, including guardrails to ensure AI usage improves output quality and velocity rather than introducing risk or degrading craft.
  
  

* Identifies and removes friction in how engineering work gets done company-wide, streamlining processes that slow every team down in the same way. • Is the ultimate accountable owner for engineering management practice (how EMs lead, how performance is evaluated, how the craft is grown) even where day-to-day people management is embedded in product teams. Impact: Engineering quality, velocity, and management practice don't fragment by product line. An engineer's experience of "how we build software here" is consistent no matter which team they're on, and the org gets the benefits of scale (shared tooling, shared standards) instead of each team reinventing its own.

SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE • Engineers across the organization deliver flawless technical execution that earns long-term client retention and supports growth. • Product lines are resourced against strategic priority, with tradeoffs made explicitly rather than by default. • Engineering leads across product lines operate with a shared technical bar and shared tooling. • Company-wide initiatives (QA automation, AI usage standards) ship and get adopted, not just get designed.
  
  

* Engineering management practice is consistent and healthy across the org, even though EMs are embedded in product teams day to day. QUALIFICATIONS Maestro hires for demonstrated capability, not years-of-service checkboxes. The bar below is competency-based: what someone needs to be able to do, not how long they've been doing it. Required competencies: • Has personally carried end-to-end accountability for engineering delivery across more than one product or team simultaneously: not just led a single team, but balanced competing priorities across several.
* Can translate ambiguous, high-level strategy (from product, business, or leadership) into a technical execution plan that engineers can actually build against, without needing someone else to do that translation. • Has designed or materially improved an engineering standard, process, or tooling investment that worked across teams (not a single-team fix) and can point to the before/after. • Comfortably operates in a matrixed environment, influencing and aligning engineering leads, their teams, and cross-functional stakeholders without relying on formal authority. • Has hands-on technical depth sufficient to earn credibility with senior engineers and to personally evaluate technical tradeoffs.

This is not a purely managerial role. • Has direct experience managing or mentoring engineering managers, not only individual contributors. • Demonstrates sound judgment on when to standardize company-wide versus when to let product teams operate with autonomy. Strongly preferred: • Experience operating at this scope inside a company of comparable size (roughly 15 to 50 engineers), where formal process is lighter and judgment calls happen more often than policy lookups.
  
  

* Direct experience setting a company's approach to AI-assisted engineering (tooling choices, guardrails, or usage standards) rather than just using AI tools personally. • A track record of building or scaling QA automation, testing strategy, or release process across multiple teams. • Experience partnering directly with Product and Delivery leadership as a peer, not just receiving requirements from them. • Experience leading engineering for always-on, customer-facing digital products or live-service platforms, where availability, release discipline, observability, incident response, and rapid cross-functional coordination directly affect the end-user experience and client retention.

**What we're explicitly not requiring:** • A specific prior title (VP Engineering, CTO, etc.). We care about scope actually carried, not the title it came with. • A minimum years-of-experience threshold. Competency and evidence of impact matter more than tenure.
  
  

* Deep expertise in every technology in Maestro's stack. Technical judgment and the ability to evaluate tradeoffs matter more than hands-on fluency in any one language or framework.

The Head of Enterprise Architecture (HEA) is responsible for establishing and leading Medica's enterprise architecture organization and ensuring Medica’s enterprise architecture aligns and enables, our business strategy, operating capabilities, technology, data, and processes, resulting in measurable and increasing enterprise value. Reporting directly to the Chief Information Officer, the HEA serves as a strategic advisor to the CIO and senior business and technology leaders and leads a multidisciplinary architecture organization spanning enterprise, business, security, data, integration, and related architecture disciplines. The HEA also leads an enterprise-wide Architecture Community of Practice to align architects and architecture-adjacent roles around common principles, standards, methods, patterns, and decision practices.

Business Architecture is a foundational discipline of the practice. The HEA ensures a clear understanding of enterprise business objectives, the current and required state of business capabilities, and the value-aligned roadmaps needed to move from current to target state. These roadmaps integrate changes across technology, data, processes, organization, skills, and operating models. The role partners closely with the Office of the CIO, Enterprise Transformation, Business Process Re-engineering, Product Ownership, Engineering, Data, Security, and business leadership to translate strategy into executable change.

The HEA will evolve Enterprise Architecture from a traditional, centralized governance model toward an enabling, embedded, and delivery-oriented practice. Architecture will engage earlier and more deeply in strategic and day-to-day delivery, using reusable standards, reference architectures, patterns, guardrails, and risk-based decision frameworks to accelerate sound decisions. The HEA will also advance AI-enabled architecture practices to automate routine documentation, analysis, standards validation, knowledge management, and governance activities so architects can focus on solving critical business problems, transformation, complex design decisions, and delivery enablement.

**Key Accountabilities**

**Structure and Advance Enterprise Architecture Practices**

* Establish and continuously evolve the enterprise architecture strategy, operating model, principles, standards, methods, and practices.
* Establish Business Architecture as the connective layer between enterprise strategy, transformation, product portfolios, business processes, organizational design, data, and technology.
* Ensure development and maintenance of enterprise business capability models; partner to assess current-state maturity and identify capability gaps, dependencies, duplication, and investment needs.
* Translate enterprise strategy and business objectives into target states, transition states, and value-aligned capability roadmaps integrating changes to people, process, technology, data, organization, skills, and operating models.
* Provide enterprise leaders with clear views of strategic dependencies, tradeoffs, sequencing, technical health, and investment implications.
* Ensure technology strategy is traceable to business strategy and capability requirements.

**Deliver Enterprise Transformation & Strategy through Architecture**

* Serve as a strategic architecture advisor to the CIO, executive leadership, Transformation, Product, and business leaders.
* Partner with Enterprise Transformation and Business Process Re-engineering to connect strategic objectives, transformation portfolios, and process redesign to required business-capability changes.
* Partner with Product Owners and Product Management to connect enterprise capability roadmaps with product strategies, investment priorities, and delivery roadmaps.
* Ensure architecture strategy reflects the operating, regulatory, data, and interoperability requirements of a healthcare organization, with particular emphasis on the health plan/payer environment.
* Provide architectural leadership for healthcare interoperability and industry standards, including X12 EDI, HL7 FHIR, USCDI, and other applicable healthcare information-exchange standards.
* Translate regulatory and interoperability requirements into enterprise capabilities and strategic roadmaps in partnership with Compliance, Legal, Security, Privacy, Product, Data, and business leaders.

**Architecture Enablement & Governance**

* Modernize the Architecture Review process from a primarily centralized approval mechanism into a risk-based architecture enablement model embedded earlier in strategy, discovery, design, and delivery.
* Establish reference architectures, reusable patterns, standards, guardrails, decision frameworks, and architecture decision records that increase delivery autonomy while maintaining enterprise alignment.
* Define clear decision rights across Enterprise Architecture, domain architecture, solution architecture, Engineering, Product, Security, Data, and related functions.

* Use AI and automation to improve architecture knowledge discovery, documentation, standards validation, impact analysis, dependency identification, and governance workflows, freeing architects for higher-value work.
* Measure architecture effectiveness through business outcomes, delivery enablement, reuse, simplification, risk reduction, technology health, and decision quality.

* Lead, develop, and mentor a multidisciplinary architecture organization spanning enterprise, business, security, data, integration, and related architecture disciplines.
* Establish and lead an enterprise-wide Architecture Community of Practice encompassing architects and architecture-adjacent roles across centralized and distributed teams.

* Develop architecture talent, competency models, career paths, succession plans, and leadership capability across the enterprise.

Power Factors is scaling in complexity — more products, more platforms, more sophisticated buyers, and rapidly rising expectations for AI-native capability across our renewable energy software suite. **ABOUT NEQ OPERATING**
=======================

NEQ Operating is a leading operator of upstream oil and gas assets across the Lower 48, managing a diversified, multi-basin portfolio that includes assets in South Texas, Haynesville and the Mid-Continent. Backed by Quantum Capital Group and NextEra Energy Resources, NEQ is building a scaled, world-class upstream business through the strategic acquisition, development and optimization of PDP-heavy, yield-oriented assets.

**ROLE SUMMARY**
================

The Director, Information Technology is NEQ’s senior technology and data leader and a key member of the executive leadership team, reporting directly to the Chief Operating Officer. The role owns executing the technology agenda for an independent upstream operator: strategic partnerships, business applications, data and analytics, AI, infrastructure and cloud, field and operational technology, end-user devices and cybersecurity.

NEQ treats data and technology as a strategic asset. This leader will build a lean, high-performing function, with leads for Data/Analytics/AI, Operational Technology / Engineering Technology (OT/ET) and IT, that turns operational, subsurface, land and financial data into faster and better-informed decisions, using a deliberate blend of in-house talent and best-in-class partners. The role is equal parts strategist, builder and operator. This position is based in Houston, Texas or Oklahoma City, Oklahoma.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**
========================

* **Technology and data strategy:** Develop and own a multi-year technology and data strategy and roadmap aligned to NEQ’s operating plan, development program, capital discipline and continuous optimization of the business; serve as the COO’s principal advisor on technology, data and digital opportunities.

* **Governance and value:** Establish technology and data governance, including project portfolio prioritization, architecture standards and decision rights with business leaders; build business cases and cost/benefit analyses, and report on realized value.

* **Data foundation:** Lead the design of a trusted, well-governed data platform that integrates drilling and completions, production, subsurface, land, marketing and financial data into a single, authoritative version of the truth, with data ownership, quality standards and master data management for wells, properties, owners, vendors, contracts and AFEs.

* **Decision support:** Partner with Operations, Subsurface, Land, Engineering and Finance as co-owners of analytics priorities, delivering self-service reporting, dashboards and advanced analytics, such as production surveillance, cost per well and capital performance.

* **AI and automation:** Work hand in hand with business domain leaders to evaluate and responsibly deploy AI, machine learning and automation where they create measurable operational or financial value.

* **Business applications:** Own the upstream application portfolio, including ERP and financials, revenue and joint interest accounting, production accounting, land and division order systems, field data capture, and geoscience and engineering tools; lead selection, implementation, integration and lifecycle management, avoiding unnecessary customization and rationalizing redundant systems.

* **Business partnership:** Partner with Finance, Land, Operations, Subsurface and Marketing leaders to ensure systems support end-to-end processes and the control environment.

* **Engineering and operational technology:** Oversee SCADA, measurement, automation and field connectivity in partnership with Operations, ensuring reliable and secure data flow from the wellhead to the enterprise; drive IT/OT convergence, including field network architecture, remote monitoring, edge data capture and asset-level technology standards.

* **Infrastructure and service delivery:** Be accountable for the network, cloud, end-user computing, collaboration and telecommunications environments that support office and field personnel; set and manage service levels, maintain disaster recovery and business continuity plans appropriate to a producing operator, and oversee technology asset inventories.

* **Cybersecurity, risk and compliance:** Own the cybersecurity program, including risk assessment, threat monitoring and incident response; establish and enforce technology policies and procedures, and ensure IT general controls and audit readiness supporting financial reporting, lender and investor requirements.

* **Vendors and financial management:** Plan and manage the technology operating and capital budgets with transparent forecasting and cost discipline suited to a lean organization; negotiate and manage technology contracts and relationships with systems integrators, managed-service providers and software vendors, holding them accountable for performance and outcomes.

* **Transaction and separation support:** Plan and manage the technology portion of acquisitions, divestitures and integrations, including diligence, Day 1 readiness and post-close consolidation; lead technology separation activities for a newly independent company, including exit from transition services, system cutovers and standalone capability build.

* **People and organization:** Design and lead a lean, high-caliber team and an operating model that blends core employees with strategic partners and the business; recruit, develop and retain top talent, and set a culture of accountability, clear communication, security awareness and continuous improvement.

**QUALIFICATIONS**
==================

**Required**

* Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Management Information Systems, Engineering, or a business degree with a technology concentration.

* Fifteen or more years of progressive IT experience, including at least eight years leading teams and managing budgets at a Director, VP or CIO level.

* Demonstrated success building data and analytics capabilities that changed how an organization makes decisions, including data governance, architecture and business intelligence.

* Working knowledge of oil and gas processes and applications, including finance and accounting, land, production operations and subsurface.

* Experience leading ERP or core business system implementations and integrating a multi-vendor application landscape.

* Solid technical understanding of infrastructure, cloud, network, operating systems and security, plus familiarity with SCADA, measurement and field connectivity.

* Proven experience managing outsourcing providers and third-party services, including contract negotiation and performance management.

* Availability to IT staff and business leaders five days per week, 7 AM to 7 PM, and on call 24/7 for critical incidents; ability to travel periodically to field offices, facilities and well sites, with required safety training and personal protective equipment.

**Preferred**

* MBA or advanced degree (MS).

* Significant experience in upstream exploration and production, including finance and accounting, land, production operations and subsurface.

* Experience with acquisitions, divestitures or carve-outs, and standing up IT for a new or independent entity.

* Executive presence and the ability to explain technology and data in business terms to operations, finance and board-level audiences.

* Strategic and analytical mindset paired with a hands-on, pragmatic approach suited to a lean organization, with strong judgment on build versus buy, standardization versus customization, and risk versus speed.

* Collaborative leadership style, with the ability to influence peers and earn credibility with field and office teams alike.

At Compass, our mission is to help everyone find their place in the world. Founded in 2012, we're revolutionizing the real estate industry with our end-to-end platform that empowers residential real estate agents to deliver exceptional service to seller and buyer clients.

**About Compass International Holdings**

Compass International Holdings is the largest residential real estate brokerage in the United States by sales volume. Founded in New York City in 2012 by Robert Reffkin and Ori Allon, and publicly traded on the NYSE, Compass was built on a simple premise: real estate agents are the heart of the transaction, and great technology makes them dramatically more effective.

Following the combination with Anywhere Real Estate, Compass International Holdings operates a portfolio of the most recognized brands in the industry — including Compass, Coldwell Banker, Sotheby's International Realty, Corcoran, Century 21, and ERA — supporting a combined network of over 300K agents across approximately 120 countries and territories.

What makes Compass International Holdings unusual in this industry is that we build our own software. Our end-to-end Home Platform, the Compass One client dashboard, and our AI assistant are developed in-house by engineering teams across New York, Seattle, Boston, and Miami. Technology is not a support function here; it is the product that differentiates the company. That is what makes infrastructure a first-class concern — and it is the premise of this role. Just as Compass makes agents more effective, Technical Infrastructure exists to make our Product and Engineering teams more effective.

**About the Role**

As Director of Engineering for Technical Infrastructure, you will own the platform that every engineer at Compass builds on. Tech Infra's mission is to empower our engineers to build, test, and ship high-quality software with maximum speed and confidence by providing a reliable, cost-effective "Golden Path" of centralized tools that eliminates operational complexity so product teams can focus on innovation. You will be accountable for that mission across compute, networking, databases, streaming, build and release systems, test infrastructure, observability, developer tooling, and the AI-enabled software development lifecycle. You will support a footprint that today spans more than 1,400 services, hundreds of managed datastores, and thousands of engineers' daily workflows.

This is a manager-of-managers role in a functional area with an expectation to shape the infrastructure architecture and technology strategy for years to come. You will own a domain where the business problem is not always defined for you and the technology strategy could be genuinely open — where part of the job is determining what the right problem is before committing the organization to solving it. You will set the high-level vision and long-term direction, make the case for resourcing initiatives that span multiple years, and take on the endemic problems that have resisted easier fixes. You will be trusted with goals that matter at the company level, and judged on outcomes rather than activity.

You will establish and evolve scalable team structures, recognizing when to create a team, when to hire a specialized role, and when teams should combine for a better outcome. You will demonstrate frugality by prioritizing the initiatives that achieve the greatest impact for the least resource, and by driving down the places where the organization applies the same engineering effort year after year. You will retain a strategic focus while staying close enough to the technology to ask the hard questions — where do we bottleneck the business, and should this system continue to exist at all. You will build closed-loop mechanisms that tell you quickly when an initiative is at risk, and act decisively.

Above all, this is a leadership role. You will grow Engineering Managers and senior technical leaders through coaching, strategic project assignment, and genuine delegation of ownership. You will partner with Principal Engineers on the decisions that outlive any single roadmap, give credit visibly, own results in both directions, and build an organization that is better for your presence but does not depend on it.

**Responsibilities**

* **Own the Infrastructure Vision:** Set the long-term technical direction for the Golden Path across cloud platform, build and release, data infrastructure, developer experience, and the AI-enabled software development lifecycle. Make the case for multi-year investment and decide what we improve, invent, deprecate, or simplify.
* **Lead and Develop Leaders:** Manage, coach, and grow a team of Engineering Managers and senior technical leaders, and may directly manage one or two high-impact teams in a critical technology area. Build succession depth, develop and promote top performers, and handle complex people situations with judgment.
* **Design the Organization:** Structure teams to encapsulate technology areas cleanly so that customer, business, and technology needs are met. Recognize when to create a team, when to hire specialized roles, and when teams should combine for a better outcome.
* **Drive Reliability and Deployment Safety:** Reduce the blast radius and duration of production failures for every customer. Hold the organization to incident, time-to-resolution, and availability targets, and establish mechanisms that make regressions visible before they reach production.
* **Own Cost Discipline at Scale:** Shape and execute infrastructure cost-optimization strategy across the organization — setting reduction targets, establishing tracking metrics, forecasting accurately, and evaluating the cost-benefit of new projects and technologies against business objectives.
* **Accelerate Developer Productivity:** Treat internal engineers as customers. Drive build speed and reliability, test infrastructure quality, AI-assisted development adoption, and tooling maturity — and attack recurring operational toil wherever the organization spends the same engineering effort year after year.
* **Communicate Strategically:** Drive high-level written and verbal communication across senior leadership — tenets, architectural plans, planning documents, and business reviews — and input into company-level technical OKR planning.

**Requirements**

* **Strong Technical Background:** 12+ years of software engineering experience with deep infrastructure or platform depth — cloud architecture, distributed systems, build and release engineering, managed data platforms, or large-scale operations.
* **Manager of Managers:** 8+ years of engineering management experience including proven success hiring, developing, and promoting Engineering Managers, and leading senior and staff-level ICs and geographically distributed teams.
* **Infrastructure Platform Ownership:** A track record owning a large, shared technology surface used by other engineering organizations, with demonstrated ability to drive adoption and standards across teams you do not control.
* **Cloud and Cost Fluency:** Strong command of AWS (GCP a plus) and the economics underneath it — commitment and savings-plan strategy, compute elasticity, instance and processor migrations, and cost observability as a first-class architectural concern.
* **Operational Excellence:** Demonstrated ability to set and hit reliability and operational targets at scale, with real experience in incident management, observability, progressive delivery, and root-cause-driven remediation.
* **Comfort with Ambiguity:** A self-starter who can take an undefined business problem and open technology strategy and produce a structured, phased, resourced plan — and who distinguishes clearly between one-way and two-way doors.
* **Security and Compliance Aptitude:** Solid understanding of enterprise security concepts including IAM, zero-trust and service-to-service authorization, least privilege, data isolation, and regula

**Position Description**

The Contract Operations Manager oversees the day-to-day management of personnel assigned to client contracts, including scheduling, shift coverage, timesheets, time-off requests, onboarding, offboarding, and routine personnel matters. The position ensures adequate staffing and smooth contract operations through staff supervision, client coordination, and onsite visits. The role serves as the primary operational liaison between the organization, its contract personnel, and assigned clients, and works with Human Resources on matters requiring formal personnel action.

Some assigned contracts operate on a 24-hour schedule. While the position generally follows standard business hours, occasional evening availability may be necessary for phone or virtual meetings, communicating updates, or checking in with personnel working night shifts. Routine overnight onsite visits are not required.

This is an operational management position focused on personnel, staffing, and client coordination, not contract administration, drafting, or procurement. It requires strong interpersonal skills, sound judgment, and the ability to navigate sensitive client relationships, address challenging personalities, and resolve concerns diplomatically while maintaining professional boundaries and representing the organization's interests.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

**Scheduling and Shift Coverage**

* Develop, publish, and maintain staff schedules for assigned contracts.
* Coordinate shift changes, coverage, and time-off requests to maintain required staffing levels.

* Review and approve timesheets and routine time-off requests.
* Address scheduling conflicts, unexpected absences, and last-minute coverage needs.
* Monitor staffing levels and proactively identify potential coverage issues, including after-hours needs.
* Coordinate occasional after-hours phone or virtual meetings to communicate updates, address concerns, or check in with personnel working evening or overnight shifts.

  

**Personnel Management**

* Serve as the primary point of contact for day-to-day staff questions, concerns, and requests.
* Provide routine supervision and oversight of assigned contract personnel.
* Conduct employee check-ins and address routine performance, attendance, and workplace concerns.
* Conduct annual employee performance evaluations and provide ongoing performance feedback.
* Address performance and conduct issues in accordance with the organization's progressive disciplinary process, including documenting concerns, conducting corrective conversations, and coordinating with Human Resources as appropriate.
* Coordinate employee onboarding and offboarding for assigned contracts, working with Human Resources and other internal departments to ensure required processes are completed.
* Assist with staffing changes, employee transitions, and communication of personnel changes to clients.

  

**Onsite Operational Oversight**

* Conduct periodic onsite visits to monitor staffing, performance, and overall contract operations.
* Interact with personnel to identify and address operational concerns.
* Verify attendance, schedule adherence, and compliance with site expectations.
* Ensure staff understand and follow organizational policies, client requirements, and operational procedures.
* Report significant concerns and recommend corrective actions to leadership.
* Conduct onsite visits primarily during normal business hours. After-hours or overnight onsite visits are generally not required and would only be expected in exceptional circumstances involving an urgent operational need or emergency.

  

**Communication and Client Relations**

* Serve as the primary operational liaison between the organization and assigned contract clients.
* Maintain regular communication with client representatives regarding staffing, personnel, scheduling, and operational matters.
* Attend client meetings and communicate relevant updates, decisions, and action items to internal leadership and assigned personnel.
* Coordinate communication between clients, contract personnel, Human Resources, and internal management.
* Communicate organizational updates, policy changes, and expectations to assigned personnel.
* Navigate sensitive client relationships and address difficult or contentious situations with professionalism, tact, and sound judgment.
* Balance client expectations with organizational policies and the fair treatment of assigned personnel, advocating for the organization's interests while resolving concerns diplomatically.
* Attend internal management meetings and provide updates on staffing, performance, client concerns, and contract operations.
* Maintain accurate staffing records and prepare reports on schedules, coverage, attendance, and other relevant performance metrics.

  

**Additional Responsibilities**

* Support the onboarding and operational transition of additional contracts as the position expands.
* Perform other duties as assigned.

  

**Required Qualifications**

* Experience supervising or managing employees, preferably in a field-based or multi-site environment.
* Experience coordinating staff schedules, shift coverage, and time-off requests.
* Experience with employee onboarding, offboarding, and personnel coordination.
* Experience managing personnel in a 24-hour or shift-based operational environment.
* Experience conducting performance evaluations, documenting performance concerns, and addressing employee conduct issues.
* Strong communication, organizational, interpersonal, and problem-solving skills.
* Demonstrated ability to handle challenging conversations, navigate sensitive client relationships, and manage competing expectations with professionalism, tact, and sound judgment.
* Ability to address routine personnel issues and recognize matters requiring escalation to Human Resources.
* Experience communicating with clients and maintaining professional working relationships.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office and scheduling, timekeeping, or workforce management systems.
* Ability to travel to assigned contract locations for periodic onsite visits.

* Flexibility to occasionally participate in evening phone or virtual meetings to accommodate personnel working alternate shifts.

  

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Prior experience in operations management, workforce scheduling, personnel supervision, or contract personnel oversight.
* Experience supporting a staff of fifteen or more employees across multiple worksites or shifts.
* Prior experience working within a Managed Service Provider (MSP) or contract staffing environment.

This position primarily operates during standard business hours but requires flexibility to support contracts operating on a 24-hour schedule. At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.
  
  
As a Senior Technical Account Manager (Senior TAM, L6) at Affirm, you will own the operational aspect of technical account management across Affirm's strategic alliance portfolio—alerting, monitoring, troubleshooting, delivering against SLAs, fielding technical inquiries, and performing investigations and analysis, while also driving technical initiatives that translate merchant business objectives into technical strategies and product optimizations. Senior TAMs are part of the Engineering team and collaborate closely with Affirm's Product, Engineering, Operations, Customer Success, and Frontline Technical Support teams.
  
  
This is an operations-heavy role to start. Expect the majority of your early focus to be on keeping merchant integrations healthy—monitoring, triage, troubleshooting, and SLA delivery—while you progressively take on more custom solutioning and cross-functional initiatives. Over your first 6–12 months, as you build operational mastery, you will grow into owning your own book of accounts and carrying it through to end-to-end account ownership.
  
  
A Senior TAM independently owns operational health across the strategic alliance portfolio, designs custom integration solutions grounded in Affirm's standard integrations, drives cross-team collaboration on initiatives, acts as a technical lead on team projects, and mentors less-experienced members of the team.
  
  
What You'll Do
  
  

* Own the operational aspect of technical account management across Affirm's strategic alliance portfolio—alerting, monitoring, troubleshooting, and fielding technical inquiries—so integrations stay healthy and issues are resolved quickly.
* Deliver against SLAs, proactively surfacing technical risks before they become customer-impacting and responding with urgency to merchant issues.
* Perform in-depth investigations and root-cause analysis across logs, queries, and integration data, owning resolution end to end and escalating to cross-functional partners or executives when needed.
* Drive technical initiatives and partner with internal and merchant stakeholders on launch initiatives—expansions, promotions, new product adoption, and integration optimizations—that grow the value of the accounts after launch.
* Design and deliver high-scope, often-custom integration solutions grounded in Affirm's standard integrations—combining, extending, and tailoring them to complex, open-ended problems while balancing speed, quality, maintainability, reliability, and scalability.
* Act as a technical lead for internal projects, defining and delivering well-scoped milestones and executing the project roadmap.
* Operationalize best practices by creating and updating playbooks, runbooks, alerting, and UAT certification plans across the strategic alliance portfolio and continuously reduce keep-the-lights-on (KTLO) work.
* Partner with Product and Engineering leads to identify, plan, and prioritize projects based on team goals and resources, acting as the voice of the merchant to influence the roadmap.
* Mentor and level up less-experienced TAMs, share learnings from your integrations and investigations, and contribute to interviewing and team development.
* Over your first 6–12 months, grow into owning a dedicated book of strategic alliance accounts—carrying operational ownership through to end-to-end account ownership.

What We Look For
  
  

* Professional Background: at least six years in a technical, external-facing role such as Technical Account Management, Solutions/Partner Engineering, or Solutions Architecture—ideally within FinTech, payments, or SaaS—with a demonstrated track record of owning the operational health of technical accounts and delivering against SLAs.
* Operational Ownership: proven ability to run alerting, monitoring, troubleshooting, and technical inquiries across a set of accounts, balancing reactive operational work with proactive initiatives.
* Ownership & Autonomy: proven ability to independently scope and deliver complex, open-ended technical work, and to partner with stakeholders on launch initiatives, with strong project management and follow-through.
* API Expertise: deep understanding of RESTful APIs, webhooks, and the HTTP protocol, with hands-on experience using tools like Postman to debug and validate integrations.
* Architecture Fluency: Experience in API integrations and the ability to design custom solutions on top of them to solve complex merchant challenges.
* Coding & Code Fluency: ability to read and understand production-level code (HTML, JavaScript, SQL, and ideally one server-side language such as Python) and to author new, novel queries to diagnose merchant or system issues.
* Troubleshooting Acumen: ability to diagnose issues using browser developer consoles, log analysis and observability platforms (e.g., Snowflake, Chronosphere), and ticketing systems (e.g., Jira, Notion).
* Technical Communication: excellent verbal and written communication; able to tailor explanations to both non-technical leaders and technical teams, read a room and adjust in real time, and synthesize technical challenges back to internal teams.
* Relationship Management: ability to discover and develop relationships with technical decision-makers, secure written consensus on integration milestones, and drive cross-team collaboration.
* Leadership & Mentorship: demonstrated ability to mentor teammates, set best practices, and lead technical initiatives; a growth mindset with self-awareness and a habit of seeking and acting on feedback.

Nice to Have
  
  

* Familiarity with the payments ecosystem.
* Familiarity with web/mobile application architecture.
* Experience implementing or customizing e-commerce platforms, payment gateways, or in-store point-of-sale systems.
* Experience acting as a technical lead on cross-functional projects and influencing product roadmaps.

### **Job Description**

**Position Summary:**  
Reporting directly to the Chief Operating Officer, the Director, LNG Strategic Delivery is responsible for leading the corporate and cross-functional workstreams that support enterprise-wide operational readiness. This role owns integration planning from LNG operations to IT, HR, finance, procurement, supply chain, safety, security, and legal. This role interfaces heavily with those functions along with corporate leadership. Engineering-focused RFO activities sit with the Manager, RFO Operations, who leads site- and asset-level readiness under the VP of Operations — the two roles partner closely to keep corporate integration efforts and field readiness activities aligned. The candidate will also possess a deep understanding of the fundamentals of engineering/project management with a breadth of knowledge in contracting, risk, and interface management as well. * Build and maintain integration plans that align corporate workstreams with organizational goals, including timelines, milestones, and resource requirements.

* Partner with Safety, Security, HR, Finance, Procurement, IT, and other corporate teams to ensure integration initiatives support overall business objectives.

* Identify integration risks, propose mitigation approaches, and help ensure compliance with relevant regulations and industry practices.
* Support budgeting, forecasting, and financial reporting for integration-related workstreams, and flag opportunities for cost optimization. ·
* Track and report on integration progress against defined success metrics; escalate risks to the COO as needed.
* Help adapt integration plans in response to technological change, market shifts, and evolving business needs.
* Expand the breadth of the organization’s future developments ·
* Ensure gaps between operations, engineering and construction are filled timely. ·
* Ensure future developments are aligned with corporate strategy and well defined. ·
* Other activities as directed by the Chief Operating Officer to achieve the business strategy and strategic deliverables for the corporation.

*Education, Certificates, and Licenses:*

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, or a related discipline.

*Experience:*

* 15+ years of experience in project management, strategy, digital transformation, or operational program management, ideally within oil and gas or a related industrial sector.
* Relevant experience may also include prior work on LNG Ready-for-Operations (RFO) or comparable large-scale capital project start-ups.

*Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:*

* Strong communication and coordination skills, with the ability to work across corporate, operations, and field stakeholders.
* Working knowledge of business strategy, operational processes, and digital/IT integration.
* Familiarity with safety, asset integrity, and maintenance management systems as they relate to readiness planning.
* Experience developing or supporting operational procedures and readiness metrics.
* Results-focused, with the ability to manage multiple concurrent workstreams and work effectively across corporate, operations, and field stakeholders.
* Demonstrated comfort operating in a lean organization with less formal structure than a large, established operator.
* Self-starter who takes ownership without close direction, and proactively identifies gaps, risks, or misalignment across workstreams before they become problems.
* Highly organized, with the discipline to track numerous concurrent, interdependent deliverables against a fixed timeline without losing sight of detail.
* Strong understanding of lump-sum, turn-key EPC execution workflows, including interface management, change control, and construction turnover processes.

This position is responsible for leadership of the faculty services and support unit of the college’s online unit, NOVA Online. * Work with Liaisons, Deans and Vice Presidents from 22 VCCS Partner colleges to ensure quality delivery of NOL courses.

* Assist senior administrators with access to faculty credentials for accreditation purposes.
* Train new liaisons and oversee all administration of SSDL courses including SIS coding, coding errors, billing, and communication with Liaisons.

LawnStarter is the nation's leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and outdoor services, spanning three brands: LawnStarter, Lawn Love, and Home Gnome. We've cleared $750M in bookings and turned a profit three years running. Founded in Austin in 2013, we're a team of about 180 that scales past 500 employees during peak season. The marketplace itself is easy to describe and hard to run well: a customer requests a service, we price the job and match it to an eligible Pro, the Pro claims and completes the work, and we process payment and take a commission.

We're entering the most ambitious stretch in the company's history as we build new verticals, new software products, and the groundwork to become a multi-billion-dollar company.

One of our company values is AI or Extinction: every task, AI-first. No exceptions, no excuses. Top 1% or we're already a fossil. This role is hired against that bar.

**The Role**

This is a biz ops generalist role, built for someone who wants to work across many parts of the business instead of owning one narrow lane. You'll start as an individual contributor with no direct reports, in a new seat reporting directly to the COO. Your first owned area will be building Service Delivery into a working operational function. This will entail adding structure, visibility and process to the way we ensure as many customer jobs as possible are completed successfully and on time by LawnStarter Pros, in lawn care and other services we offer now and over time.

New projects will show up unscoped over time. That's by design. As LawnStarter enters new verticals and grows toward a multi-billion-dollar future, big problems will keep surfacing with no obvious owner, and you'll be one of the people the COO trusts to run them down.

**What makes this role different:**

* You work on some of the biggest company-wide projects, cutting across teams and functional areas.
* You'll be a top builder in Brain, LawnStarter's internal AI toolkit built on Claude Code that already powers everything we do across the company: metric queries, document drafting, bug triage, and more. We expect you to approach your work in an AI-first fashion, leveraging Brain to build new systems and processes that will push the limits of how fast AI can accelerate business results. Every project you run is built AI-first: the analysis, the tooling, the process automation, the monitoring. You build it yourself instead of waiting on an analyst or engineer.
* You own outcomes end to end, from recommendation through execution. Strategy without follow-through doesn't count here.

**What You'll Own**

* **Service Delivery, from the ground up.** Despite LawnStarter's considerable scale and reach, Service Delivery doesn't exist yet as a dedicated function. You'll help define the standards we should meet for job completion rates and speed, measure whether we hit them, and design processes, incentives and real-time interventions that get tested with Pros and customers in the field to lift performance. Scope covers every vertical and every delivery model, from today's 1099 Pros to potential W-2 crews under future evaluation.
* **Raising customer & Pro retention rates.** When we deliver service with excellence, Pros and customers alike stay with us longer. Working tightly with peers across Product, Data and Support, you'll identify new opportunities for us to boost retention and LTV and play a key role in driving resulting initiatives cross-functionally.
* **Whatever comes next.** New projects will land on your plate as the company grows into new verticals and builds new software products. You'll take them from "we should look into this" to building and then running systems with structure, KPIs and owners.

**Problems to Solve**

**Build a Service Delivery function that doesn't exist yet.** Right now, no one formally owns whether LawnStarter delivers the service it promises. You'll define the standard for what a Pro should deliver, then build the agents and pipelines that measure adherence to it and run the tests that change behaviors and outcomes in the field.

**Move metrics.** Leverage systems thinking and AI expertise to drive business results that sit across various functional teams. That means untangling handoffs where several teams touch a problem or goal and no one team owns the outcome.

The Quality Assurance Manager is the strategic leader responsible for overseeing and elevating an organization’s quality management systems. This role involves defining, implementing, and monitoring quality standards to ensure products or services meet internal benchmarks, industry regulations, and customer expectations. Acting as both a process improvement advocate and a compliance expert, the Quality Assurance Manager guides cross-functional teams through regular audits, evaluations, and corrective initiatives to sustain operational excellence and drive continuous improvement. This leadership classification requires a proactive approach, advanced analytical skills, and an in-depth understanding of both regulatory requirements and industry best practices.

**Primary Responsibilities**

Ensure the quality management system aligns with industry standards (e.g., International Organization for Standardization, Good Manufacturing Practice, Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points, etc.) and regulatory requirements. Coordinate corrective and preventive actions based on audit findings to reduce risks and improve quality performance. Manage, mentor, and develop the quality assurance team to build expertise and ensure strong adherence to quality protocols. Collaborate with production, engineering, product development, and supply chain teams to resolve quality issues and reinforce quality improvement initiatives. Implement metrics, dashboards, and performance indicators to track quality data and drive data-informed decision-making. Perform root cause analyses and implement sustainable improvements to reduce defects, enhance product quality, and increase operational efficiency. Work closely with suppliers and vendors to assure that raw materials and components meet established quality standards. Serve as the primary point of contact for regulatory agencies, customer audits, and quality-related inquiries. Oversee detailed documentation of quality processes, audit reports, and corrective action plans. Report quality performance trends and issues to senior management, offering actionable insights and strategic recommendations.

**Knowledge and Skills**

Proficiency in using statistical analysis tools and quality management software to interpret and manipulate quality data. A detail-oriented mindset combined with strong problem-solving abilities to identify root causes and implement effective solutions. Exceptional leadership skills with a proven ability to inspire and guide a multidisciplinary team. Strong written and verbal communication skills to effectively liaise with all levels of the organization, regulatory bodies, and external partners. Deep understanding of applicable regulations, quality standards, and industry best practices to ensure continuous compliance. The ability to stay updated on evolving standards and innovations in quality management. Skilled in managing multiple projects simultaneously, ensuring deadlines are met, and quality improvements are systematically tracked and achieved.

**Quality Control & Performance Monitoring**

* Monitor transportation services for timeliness, reliability, safety, and compliance.

* Track service performance and identify recurring problems.
* Prepare quality-control and performance reports.

* Receive, document, and investigate transportation-related complaints.
* Investigate accidents, service failures, safety concerns, and operational incidents.
* Interview drivers and other personnel when necessary.
* Review available records and supporting documentation.
* Identify contributing factors and recommend corrective actions.

* Monitor wheelchair loading, unloading, and securement practices.
* Conduct vehicle safety and cleanliness inspections.
* Identify unsafe practices and report deficiencies to management.
* Coordinate with operations personnel to address identified concerns.

**Compliance & Corrective Action**

* Monitor compliance with company policies and applicable transportation contract requirements.
* Maintain complaint logs, incident reports, inspection records, and corrective-action documentation.
* Recommend corrective measures and additional employee training when necessary.
* Track corrective actions approved by management.
* Verify that identified deficiencies have been addressed.

Wellness Equity Alliance is a national multidisciplinary health organization that designs and delivers integrated, community-based care for populations most impacted by health inequities. ### **About Wellness Equity Alliance**

Wellness Equity Alliance is a national multidisciplinary health organization that designs and delivers integrated, community-based care for populations most impacted by health inequities. We do this through mobile and field-based models, providing medical care, behavioral health services, substance use treatment, harm reduction, and care coordination in nontraditional settings such as encampments, schools, reentry sites, and rural communities, as well as with sovereign tribal nations. Grounded in trauma-informed, culturally responsive, and data-driven practices, WEA combines clinical expertise, lived experience, and advanced population health analytics to reduce barriers to care, improve continuity, and strengthen local systems. We have partnered with more than 60 public agencies, managed care plans, and community-based organizations across the U.S. to implement scalable, sustainable programs that are advancing health equity and improving outcomes for historically marginalized populations.

We are known as Renegades, Rebels, Disruptors and Dreamers. If that sounds like you, we want you on our team.

### **Overview**

Street Medicine provides direct healthcare to unhoused individuals wherever they are, with a strong focus on assessing and responding to their physical, social, and psychological needs.

Enhanced Care Management (ECM) is a statewide Medi-Cal benefit for members with complex needs. Enrolled members receive comprehensive care management from a lead care manager who coordinates all health and health-related care, including physical, mental, and dental care, as well as social services.

Community Supports (CS) are services provided by Medi-Cal managed care plans that address health-related social needs, promoting healthier lives and reducing the need for higher, costlier levels of care.

### **Position Summary**

The Street Medicine Behavioral Health Provider is a licensed or associate clinical social worker who sees patients directly in the field. As a member of WEA's multidisciplinary street medicine team, this provider delivers behavioral health assessment, treatment, and crisis care to unsheltered people experiencing homelessness and others living with serious mental illness (SMI) and substance use disorders (SUD), and carries a caseload of ECM members as their care manager.

This role is 80% field-based and 20% administrative. Field work takes place in encampments, shelters, vehicles, motels, drop-in centers, hospitals, and other community settings alongside WEA's medical providers, nurses, and community health workers. Administrative time covers documentation, care coordination, case conferences, and training.

The provider reports to the Director of Behavioral Health.

**Location:** Southern California, with field work in Los Angeles, San Bernardino, San Diego, and the Coachella Valley.

**Position type:** Full-time, hourly, or per diem.

### **Key Responsibilities**

**Direct Patient Care (Field)**

* See patients directly in the field as part of street medicine rounds, building trust with people who have often been failed by health systems.
* Conduct biopsychosocial and mental health assessments, including suicide and violence risk assessment, and make diagnoses within the provider's scope of practice and license.
* Provide brief and ongoing therapeutic interventions, including motivational interviewing, cognitive behavioral approaches, trauma-informed care, and harm reduction counseling.
* Provide crisis intervention, including de-escalation, safety planning, and coordination of emergency and psychiatric care when needed.
* Screen for and support substance use treatment, including linkage to medication for addiction treatment with WEA's medical providers.
* Support medication adherence and provide psychoeducation to patients and their support networks.
* Provide telehealth follow-up when in-person contact is not possible.

**Enhanced Care Management**

* Serve as lead care manager for an assigned caseload of ECM members, especially those with SMI or SUD and those experiencing homelessness.
* Outreach to and engage referred members, explain ECM services, and enroll members who agree to participate.
* Complete ECM assessments and develop, update, and carry out person-centered care plans that integrate behavioral health, medical, social, and housing needs.
* Coordinate care across medical, behavioral health, substance use, and social services, and close the loop on every referral.
* Make sure each member has an assigned primary care provider and support engagement with that provider.
* Support members through transitions of care, including discharges from hospitals, psychiatric facilities, and jails.
* Connect members to housing, sobering centers, substance use treatment, Community Supports, benefits, and other community resources.

**Team Collaboration**

* Serve as the behavioral health consultant to WEA's street medicine and ECM teams.
* Participate in case conferences and systematic case reviews with the multidisciplinary team.
* Work with external partners, including managed care plans, county behavioral health, shelters, hospitals, and community-based organizations.
* Provide or facilitate training for team members on behavioral health, crisis intervention, and trauma-informed care.
* Contribute to protocols, workflows, and best practices for behavioral health in street medicine.

**Documentation and Compliance (Administrative)**

* Complete timely, accurate documentation of assessments, care plans, treatment, and care coordination in the electronic health record.
* Ensure documentation supports Medi-Cal billing and meets ECM, managed care plan, and WEA standards.
* Report on patient progress and outcomes as required by contracts and WEA leadership.
* Comply with Medi-Cal, CalAIM, HIPAA, and Board of Behavioral Sciences requirements.
* Participate in quality improvement initiatives.

### **Work Environment**

This position is 80% field-based and 20% administrative. Field work takes place outdoors and in street-based settings, encampments, shelters, and community sites, in all weather conditions, with regular travel across the region.

### **Employment Conditions**

Employment is contingent on successful completion of a background check following a conditional offer of employment and on meeting WEA's Occupational Health Clearance requirements. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with the California Fair Chance Act and applicable local fair chance ordinances.

Wellness Equity Alliance does not currently accept unsolicited resumes or candidate submissions from third-party recruiters, staffing agencies, search firms, or other external recruiting vendors. Please do not contact hiring managers or members of our People & Culture team regarding recruitment services unless you have an existing agreement with WEA.

Any unsolicited resumes or candidate information submitted without a current, authorized agreement will be considered the property of Wellness Equity Alliance, and no placement fee or other compensation will be owed in connection with any resulting hire.

### **Compensation**

$85,000 - $116,000 per year for full-time positions. Hourly and per diem positions are paid at the equivalent rate.

Wellness Equity Alliance is an Equal Opportunity Employer, drug free workplace, and complies with ADA regulations as applicable.

**About The Job**
Red Hat's Technical Account Management team is looking for an enterprise-level engineer to join us remotely as an OpenShift Technical Account Manager (TAM) in the Southeastern U.S. In this role, you will work with a small set of key customers to provide direct technical and architectural guidance for the Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform. At Red Hat, customer support includes far more than just “break-fix” solutions. Customers get industry-leading resources that enable their technical environments to run efficiently, so they can focus on growing their businesses. Technical account management is a premium support offering that builds, maintains, and grows long-lasting customer loyalty between Red Hat and our customers. * Perform technical reviews and share knowledge to proactively identify and prevent issues
* Gain understanding of customer technical infrastructures, hardware, and offerings and serve as a customer advocate within Red Hat
* Collaborate with the engineering, research and development, product management, and technical support teams
* Create customer engagement plans and keep the documentation on the customer's environment updated
* Create documentation regarding customer issues and technical details on how to resolve them
* Manage and grow customer relationships by delivering attentive, relationship-based support
* Build trust with customers and serve as their advocate within Red Hat
* Forewarn customers of technology changes or potential disruptions to their service and advice on mitigation strategies.
* Provide advice and guidance to customers about their current and future Red Hat products
* Troubleshoot technical issues and drive issue escalation with Red Hat and customer teams

* Engage with Red Hat’s field teams, customers, and partners to ensure a positive cloud technology experience and a successful outcome resulting in long-term enterprise success
* Communicate how specific Red Hat cloud solutions and our cloud roadmap align to customer use cases
* Travel occasionally to visit regional customers

* 5+ years of experience working in a support, development, engineering, IT, or a quality assurance organization

* Expertise in enterprise cloud solutions like Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS), containers, Kubernetes, cloud management, and IT automation
* Ability to manage and grow existing enterprise customer relationships by delivering proactive, relationship-based support
* Competent comprehension of enterprise architecture and strategic business drivers
* Ability to manage multiple issues and projects with shifting priorities and timelines
* Outstanding written and verbal communication skills and ability to convey complex information to customers clearly and concisely in English
* Ability to travel for customer visits and events within the region
